data.name: Satis
data.gender_notes: Satis is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Goddess of Prosperity and Wife of Shiva
data.long_meaning: Satis is the goddess of fertility, marriage, prosperity, and chastity. She is the wife of Lord Shiva and is known as Parvati. Satis is also the embodiment of Shakti, the divine feminine energy. The name Satis carries the meaning “Goddess of Prosperity and Wife of Shiva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Satis usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of prosperity and wife of shiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Satis represents the divine feminine energy and is a symbol of love, devotion, and fertility.
data.etymology: Satis belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Prosperity and Wife of Shiva.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Satis total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu mythology, Satis holds a significant role as the divine consort of Lord Shiva, the god of destruction. She is also considered the personification of marital bliss, and her devotees seek her blessings for a successful marriage and motherhood.
data.spiritual_significance: Satis is a revered deity in Hinduism, symbolizing the power and strength of the feminine divine. She represents the ideals of sacrifice, devotion, and purity. Her story reflects the profound depth of love and devotion between a husband and wife. Through her divine presence and blessings, she offers guidance, strength, and fertility to her devotees on their spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sati is the embodiment of unwavering devotion and self-sacrifice in Hinduism. She is the wife of Lord Shiva and immolated herself on his pyre to protect his honor, symbolizing the highest form of marital loyalty and dedication.
